newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude holds firm, some grades firm.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude holds firm, some grades firm.

text.p: As outright North Sea Brent crude held early firmness intermonth activity was stagnant.
The market focused instead on talk of trade to the U.S. Gulf and a firming on some North Sea grades.
March Brent on the IPE had gained some 26 cents to $22.31 a barrel by 1330 GMT.

A Feb 21-23 Statfjord traded at a firm Dated Brent +50 cents on Tuesday. Two Ekofisk cargoes changed hands -- one was confirmed done at Dated +30 cents. Two Forties were heard to have moved -- one around end Feb loading was talked around Dated +44 cents, though not yet confirmed.
"This market is strong. There isn't much left even with (refining) margins not being that good," one North Sea equity holder said.
Two Brent cargoes due to load February 12-14 were being passed through the paper chains on Tuesday.

The first Statfjord left unsold now was scheduled to load off February 23, traders said. More Oseberg was seen available -- the first on February 14 but some said that early commitments meant there would not be as much as expected left unsold in the third decade.

CFD's held early firmness but activity was subdued after an early burst. Jan 28-31 heard bid at March +30 with offers five cents higher. Feb 3-7 talked around March +19/22 cents and Feb 10-14 at March +10/12 cents.
A Feb 10-12 versus Feb 17-19 roll was done at 17 cents. Feb 3-7 versus Feb 24-28 traded at +36 cents and a partial (90Kb) traded on the Feb 17-21 at April +35 cents.
Buying interest on the Brent Feb/mar spread brought levels up a few cents over the morning to +40/42 while March/April held around +40/43 cents.
